en: The Jātaka:
The Eighth Chapter, The Section on Kaccāyana (Aṭṭhakanipāta, Kaccānivagga)
3. The Sulasā Jātaka:
“This golden armlet, and many pearls and beryl gems;”
“Take everything, O Blessed One;
and announce that I am your slave.
“Lay it aside, O auspicious lady,” he said.
Do not lament so bitterly;
I do not recall ever bringing wealth here by killing anyone.”
“Since I can remember myself,
since I have reached the state of discretion,
I do not recall ever having done so.”
There is nothing dearer to me than you.
Come, I shall embrace you and perform the respectful circumambulation.
"For now there is no further meeting between me and you.
"Not indeed in all places," [he replied].
A man is wise;
a woman too is wise, discerning in every circumstance.
For it is not the case that in all circumstances a man is wise;
even a woman can be wise.
Reflecting quickly on the goal,
he indeed swiftly and promptly attained it while still nearby.
Just as Sulasā killed Sattuka with a full water-skin,
so too one who [seizes] a benefit that has arisen—
He does not awaken quickly;
that dull-witted one is destroyed like a thief in a mountain cave.
But whoever quickly understands a matter that has arisen is released from the oppression of enemies.
“Sulasā was like one desiring poison.
Thus ends the third Jātaka, the Sulasā-jātaka.
